comment: Corpus fixtures that are DELIBERATELY uncompilable.
Every other corpus file must compile and must have a baseline; the harness fails on
any file missing from both. A fixture that quietly stops compiling used to lose its
baseline and drop out of the run while the suite still reported green - which is how
the <pre><code> defect went unnoticed for months.
An entry here is not an exemption, it is an ASSERTION. Each fixture is compiled and
must fail with the recorded error. A fixture that starts compiling, or that fails
with a different message, is a regression in the parser's error reporting - which is
the only thing these fixtures exist to test.
'error' is matched as a prefix of the first line of the thrown message.
To retire an entry, fix the fixture and generate its baseline.

test-error.jqhtml.reason: Malformed on purpose - exercises the parser's error reporting.
test-error.jqhtml.error: Unbalanced bracket error in component "TestError": Unexpected token ':'

test-highlighting.jqhtml.reason: Syntax-highlighting fixture: deliberately pairs correct and incorrect forms so the VS Code grammar can be checked against both. Lines 8-9 carry quoted event handlers labelled "Wrong - String Not Function"; the parser stops at the first of them.
test-highlighting.jqhtml.error: Event attributes (@) must have unquoted values to pass function references.
